clue.text: Private school head's not initially remote

indicators.note: the head of the word school is its opening letter
not initially says the first letter of the synonym for remote is dropped

parts.note: a zapper is a TV remote control

explanation.surface: A private school's headmaster is described as not, at first, aloof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remote' looks like an adjective (distant) but is the TV zapper; losing its Z leaves APPER after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapper is a soldier of the lowest rank in the Royal Engineers, the equivalent of a private.

clue.text: At first agreed to lug old case round Englishman's castle for PM

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of the word agreed
round signals that the letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: the saying goes that an Englishman's home is his castle

explanation.surface: Someone agreed to haul an old suitcase around a castle on behalf of the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Alec Douglas-Home was British Prime Minister in 1963-64.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Alec Douglas-Home served as the UK's Prime Minister, an office abbreviated PM.

clue.text: Eg pork pie given to a model carrying little weight

indicators.note: carrying says the pie and model pieces hold the small weight inside them

parts.note: taken as written
gm is the abbreviation for gram, a small weight
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A pork pie is handed to a model who is watching her weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pork pie' tempts as a single item (or rhyming slang for lie), but 'Eg pork' is the definition and 'pie' the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigmeat is a general term for the meat of pigs, of which pork is an example.

clue.text: Eccentric characters mostly surprised by English reserve

indicators.note: surprised signals the letters are thrown into disorder
mostly says the last letter of the word Eccentric is dropped

explanation.surface: Odd characters are startled by English restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ECCENTRIC to ECCENTRI, which 'surprised' rearranges before E.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticence is a reluctance to reveal one's thoughts, so a reserved manner.

clue.text: Luggage carrier, originally from vehicle back into castle

indicators.note: into says the letters before it go inside the word for castle

parts.note: in chess the castle piece is also called a rook

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word from
back says the word for vehicle is read backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A rack for luggage, taken off the rear of a car and carried into a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'castle' suggests a fortress, but here it is the chess piece; 'Luggage carrier' could equally be a porter until the vehicle theme points to the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof rack is a frame fixed on top of a car for carrying baggage.

clue.text: Weak summary

definitions.meaning: tired and in poor health, as in feeling worn out
a quick briefing on the main points of something

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, run-down means exhausted and weak; as a noun, a rundown is a brief summary.

clue.text: Cooked topless when tipsy

indicators.note: topless says the first letter of the word for cooked is removed

parts.note: boiled is a way of being cooked

explanation.surface: Someone stripped off their top because they were tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' suggests undress but just drops the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled is informal British slang for drunk, especially slightly drunk.

clue.text: Make fresh contact with outreach organisation, after adult goes missing

indicators.note: organisation is taken as the act of arranging letters into a new order
goes missing says the letter for adult is removed

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Get back in touch with an outreach charity after an adult disappears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' reads as a body like a charity but signals rearranging OUTRECH.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whimsically as re-touch, the word suggests touching again, so contacting anew.

clue.text: Old French epic song from one of the Rat Pack?

parts.note: chanson is French for song
de is French for from
Roland Rat was a puppet star of 1980s British TV, a rat by name

explanation.surface: A song by one of Sinatra's Rat Pack, but called an old French epic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rat Pack suggests Sinatra and friends; the question mark admits it is Roland Rat, a puppet of 1980s British breakfast TV.
explanation.definitionFit: The Song of Roland is an eleventh-century French epic poem about Charlemagne's knight.

clue.text: Increase number in layer

indicators.note: in places the number inside the word for a layer

parts.note: a hen is a layer of eggs
eight is a number

explanation.surface: A farmer increases the count of birds in the laying flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' reads as a stratum, but here it is something that lays eggs: a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: To heighten is to make greater or more intense, a synonym of increase.

clue.text: A display of inexperience after cancelled service? Hatchback is deadly

indicators.note: after places the A and L pieces behind the service and the H

parts.note: in tennis a let is a serve that does not count and is replayed
the back of the word hatch is its final letter, H
L is the learner plate shown by an inexperienced driver

explanation.surface: A learner driver's hatchback after a botched service proves deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hatchback' reads as a car, fitting the L-plate picture, but it is the back letter of hatch.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethal means capable of causing death, a direct synonym of deadly.

clue.text: Tool returning chez Dad for a bit

indicators.note: returning means the run of letters is read backwards
for a bit says only a portion of the words chez Dad is used

explanation.surface: A tool is going back to Dad's place for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a cutting tool with an arched blade set at right angles to its handle.

clue.text: Downpour (cf. spurt)

parts.note: read as c and f: C stays, and f in music stands for forte, meaning loud
a spurt is a sudden burst

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry for a downpour cross-refers the reader to spurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cf.' looks like the abbreviation for compare, but it is C plus f, the musical mark for loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloudburst is a sudden, very heavy fall of rain.

clue.text: Part of Liverpool 9, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: 9 refers to the answer of 9 across

explanation.surface: A Liverpool district is given as postcode area 9.
explanation.walkthrough: Huyton is a district of Liverpool (and Harold Wilson's old seat), pronounced to rhyme with the answer to 9 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Huyton is a town on the eastern edge of Liverpool in Merseyside, so it is one part of that city area.

clue.text: New Brighton? Head off about the distance from equator given by grid reference

definitions.text: the distance from equator given by grid reference

indicators.note: about signals the remaining letters are moved around
head off says the first letter of the word Brighton is removed

explanation.surface: Is New Brighton far enough north on the map? A map reader heads off to check.
explanation.walkthrough: New Brighton is a real resort on the Wirral, tempting as a place name; 'Head off' strips the B, leaving RIGHTON, which 'about' rearranges after N.
explanation.definitionFit: On a map grid, a northing is the coordinate measuring distance northward from a base line such as the equator.

clue.text: Sort of man that can be relied on to be far from sinister

definitions.text: Sort of man that can be relied on

definitions.meaning: sinister is Latin for left, so far from it is the opposite side

explanation.definitionFit: A right-hand man is a trusted deputy; the right-hand side is the opposite of the left, sinister in heraldry.

clue.text: Two rock bands of the '70s, one halving drug use, take time showing expressiveness

parts.note: ELO, the Electric Light Orchestra, was a 1970s rock band

indicators.note: one halving says one of the pair of drug letters in the second band is dropped

parts.note: Queen was the other 1970s rock band
E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Two 1970s rock bands, one cutting back on drugs, take time to show their expressiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: QUEEN has two Es; halving its 'drug use' leaves one, QUEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fluent and persuasive in speech displays expressive power, a direct adjectival match.

clue.text: Band in which piano takes up odd bits of tune

indicators.note: takes says the word for piano holds the other letters inside

parts.note: piano in music means soft, so quiet

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters are read bottom to top, reversed
odd bits of picks the first and third letters of tune

explanation.surface: A band in which the pianist picks up stray fragments of the tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piano' is the musical direction for soft, not the instrument; in a down clue 'up' signals reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A quintet is a group of five musicians, a type of band.

clue.text: Turncoat's foremost pretext for disloyalty

indicators.note: foremost picks the first letter of Turncoat

parts.note: a pretext is a stated reason

explanation.surface: A turncoat's main excuse for betraying his side.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country, the gravest form of disloyalty.

clue.text: Threaten to go out with head of government, say

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word government

parts.note: to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A minister threatens to walk out alongside the head of government, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: A candle flame gutters when it flickers as if about to go out.
explanation.definitionFit: Of a flame, guttering is flickering weakly as though on the point of being extinguished.

clue.text: Walks wearily as a Dickensian in outskirts of Totnes

indicators.note: in puts the Dickensian character inside the edge letters
outskirts of picks the first and last letters of Totnes

parts.note: Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A Dickens character trudges around the edges of Totnes, a Devon town.
explanation.walkthrough: Totnes is a market town in Devon; its outskirts are T and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge is to walk slowly and heavily, as when tired.

clue.text: Soldier's messing about in task

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a soldier is a kind of ant; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A soldier fools about while given a job to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' suggests GI or TA, but it is the soldier ant.
explanation.definitionFit: An assignment is a piece of work allotted to someone, so a task.

clue.text: Vetoes the other trendy set-up

indicators.note: set-up in a down clue reads as set upwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: the other is a coy British euphemism for sex
in means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: Someone bans a fashionable arrangement involving the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' looks like a noun but means the whole of SEX IN is turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To nix something is informal for forbidding or cancelling it, as a veto does.

clue.text: Some oddities of uncertain recollection

indicators.note: recollection is read as collecting again in reverse, so the letters run backwards
some says only a portion of the following words is used

explanation.surface: Some odd sightings are remembered only vaguely.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: reported flying saucers are oddities that witnesses recall uncertainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Unidentified flying objects are strange sightings whose details are typically hazy in witnesses' memories.

clue.text: Almost 5 or 10, with 10 the turning point?

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
taken as written

indicators.note: almost says the last letter of the spelt-out number ten is dropped

parts.note: ten written out as a word
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Is the turning point nearly five or ten, with ten the answer?
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look like cross-references to 5 and 10 across, but are plain numbers: V, TE(n) and X.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool or whirlwind is a spinning mass, so it is literally a point around which things turn.

clue.text: Informed about husband reportedly drunk in foreign city

indicators.note: about says the first word wraps around the abbreviation for husband

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing on someone, so informed is sang

indicators.note: reportedly says the next piece is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: high can mean drunk or intoxicated

explanation.surface: Someone informed on a husband who was apparently drunk in a foreign city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Informed' is the criminal sense, singing to the police; HIGH spoken gives the last syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: Shanghai is a major city in China, foreign to the British setter.

clue.text: Get rid of black snot I produced

parts.note: jet is a deep black colour

indicators.note: produced signals the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A crude instruction to dispose of dark mucus one has produced.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw overboard or discard something unwanted.

clue.text: Foreign agreement embraced by parties in folk dance movement

indicators.note: embraced by puts the agreement inside the parties

parts.note: a do is a party, so parties gives two of them
si is yes in Spanish or Italian

explanation.surface: A foreign treaty is welcomed at parties during a folk dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A plural like 'parties' can give one short word twice, here placed either side of the foreign yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A do-si-do is a square dance figure where two dancers pass round each other back to back.
